observation_summary: The MonthDay class fails to perform arithmetic operations (plus/minus months/days) when the date is set to February 29th, throwing an IllegalFieldValueException because the underlying logic attempts to validate the day-of-month against a non-leap year range (1-28).
hypothesis: The existing implementation of BasicMonthOfYearDateTimeField.add() incorrectly attempts to reconstruct the date by iterating through fields and setting them on a default instant (0L), which defaults to a non-leap year. This causes the validation logic to reject the valid leap day (29) as out of bounds for February.
prediction: The fix will introduce a specialized path for MonthDay arithmetic that avoids the problematic reconstruction of the date on a default instant, instead performing the month-wrapping logic directly on the existing values.
experiment_rationale: The provided diff shows that a new conditional block was added to BasicMonthOfYearDateTimeField.add() to handle the month-wrapping logic specifically when the month is the largest field, bypassing the problematic loop that reconstructs the date on a default instant.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a failure in the computational strategy for handling date arithmetic on partial dates (MonthDay). The original algorithm was flawed because it forced a reconstruction of the date on a default (non-leap) year, leading to an invalid state during validation. The fix replaces this flawed procedural logic with a correct calculation for month-wrapping, which is a classic Algorithm/Method correction.
evidence_used: The stack trace shows the error occurs in BasicMonthOfYearDateTimeField.add() during field validation.
The fix diff adds a new, specialized algorithm for handling month-wrapping in BasicMonthOfYearDateTimeField.
The bug report confirms that operations on February 29th fail due to incorrect validation logic.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the error manifests as a failed check (IllegalFieldValueException), the root cause is the incorrect algorithmic approach to date reconstruction, not a missing or incorrect guard condition.
The fix is a local procedural change within an existing method, not a design-level capability correction.
